correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty W,V and the explicitly designated principal-downset core, every core-preserving map restricts to a finite Boolean-algebra morphism P(W)->P(V); it is uniquely inverse image by f:V->W. Every nonempty downset family is a finite union of principal downsets, so join preservation forces H_f(A)={T subseteq V : f[T] in A}. This formula preserves meet, join and bottom. For implication, every subset of f[T] is f[R] for some R subseteq T; this proves the needed quantifier equivalence. For tensor, any cover f[T] subseteq S union U decomposes T into two overlapping fiberwise preimages, showing tensor preservation. The image consists of exactly the downsets depending on kernel blocks of f; distinct partitions are recovered from image principal core elements, and E_Q subseteq E_P iff P refines Q. An idempotent selecting one representative of every kernel block produces every retract. Thus |E_P|=D_k-1 and the rank, automorphism and idempotent formulas follow from classical finite transformation enumeration. Boundary n=1 checked. Separate exact Python programs independently verified all 56 cross-size maps n,m<=3 for all operation pairs (57,820 assertions) and all n^n maps and partition-order/rank statistics n<=4; these finite checks do not prove the general theorem, which follows from the stated algebraic argument.

originality.rationale: The only possible incremental content is the embedded retract-image poset and Dedekind-graded enumerators, since the homomorphism normal form is already Quadrellaro Prop. 4.10/Theorem 4.11 and the dependence analogue Prop. 4.15/Theorem 4.16. But even that proposed increment follows immediately from the published categorical dualities specialized to discrete antichains: retract subalgebras correspond contravariantly to split finite-set quotients W/P, uniquely indexed by kernel partitions P; the order is opposite partition refinement. The published finite-downset model gives size D_|P|-1; elementary finite-transformation counting gives every Bell, Stirling and idempotent coefficient. BGH 2019 already gives the finite inquisitive extension H(P(W)), its normal form, and inclusions H(B0) for Boolean subalgebras B0, another direct route. This is decisive existing-theorem implication, even though earlier sources do not print the identical coefficients. No new mathematical regime or essential theorem remains; failed novelty is based on strong coverage, not on an unsuccessful search or inaccessible article.

value.rationale: Embedded retract geometry is a natural invariant for logical algebras, and an exact classification would in principle qualify. Here, however, the classification is a routine transfer of a known categorical duality to the quotient lattice of a finite set, followed by already standard Bell/Stirling/Dedekind and finite-transformation counts. There is no nonstandard obstruction, new boundary, hitherto unknown exact invariant, or new case outside the published theorem. The n=3/4 polynomials are tabulations of those formulas, and parallel treatment of the tensor signature is expressly subsumed by the earlier dependence duality. Thus scientific value of this submitted result as an original finding is not established independently of correct presentation or computational reproducibility.
risks: This verdict is about contribution beyond the earlier published structure, not about pedagogical usefulness of the explicit list.
